rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR AT LEAST TWO (2) SANGGUNIANG PANLALAWIGAN MEMBERS FOR EACH CONGRESSIONAL DISTRICT, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTION 467 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7160, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE OF 1991 AND REPEALING SECTION 2 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 6637 AND SECTION 4 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 6636, AND PROVIDING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract: Proposes the following amendment to the Local Government Code of 1991: "SEC. 467. Composition - x x x > (D) FOR PROVINCES WITH TWO (2) OR MORE LEGISLATIVE DISTRICTS, THERE SHALL BE ELECTED AT LEAST TWO (2) REGULAR MEMBERS OF THE SANGGUNIANG PANLALAWIGAN FOR EACH LEGISLATIVE DISTRICT. PROVIDED, THAT, FOR PROVINCES WITH ONLY ONE (1) LEGISLATIVE DISTRICT, THE COMMISSION ON ELECTION SHALL DIVIDE THEM INTO TWO (2) DISTRICTS FOR PURPOSES OF ELECTING THE MEMBERS OF THE SANGGUNIANG PANLALAWIGAN, AS NEARLY AS PRACTICABLE ACCORDING TO THE NUMBER OF INHABITANTS, EACH DISTRICT COMPROMISING A COMPACT, CONTIGUOUS AND ADJACENT TERRIROTY."
rows.status: Substituted by HB10479

rows.title_full: AN ACT TO REVISE THE PRESIDENTIAL DECREE NO. 797, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE MARINE POLLUTION DECREE OF 1976
rows.abstract: Rationale: The principal measure on marine pollution, that is, Presidential Decree No. 979, otherwise known as The Marine Pollution Decree of 1979, was passed in order to address problems on marine environment transpiring during those times. > It has been 18 years now since the said law was promulgated. Upheaval  of modern technologies has come to pass almost unacknowledged as we always stand in anticipation or, somewhat accustomed to their occurence. The influx of sea-transport economic activities has likewise created a considerable mileage. Monetary factors have, consequently, yielded to more ideal level. Notwithstanding these positive factors, marine environment in the Philippine Archipelago has become worst and unmanageable. Relativelyy untraced and unfetted, oily residues, garbage, wastes and other toxic elements of off-shore and land-based sources continue to plague our territorial water. "The Revised Marine Pollution Law of 1997"
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on ECOLOGY since 1997-08-05

rows.title_full: AN ACT INSTITUTING THE HEALTH MAINTENANCE ORGANIZATIONS CODE
rows.abstract: Is premised on the following objectives: (1) To recognize Health Maintenance Organizations as unique medical service providers that combine the financing, management and provision of health services and to encourage them by providing incentives; (2)To establish the regulatory framework for Health Maintenance Organizations that should protect the rights of the buying public, as well as of the various sectors involved in the delivery health care services; and (3) To make people more health conscious by making health care services readily available, accessible and affordable.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HEALTH since 1997-08-05

rows.title_full: AN ACT GIVING PRIORITY TO DIFFERENTLY-ABL ED INDIVIDUALS IN THE OPERATION OF VENDING FACILITIES IN GOVERNMENT PROPERTY, TO ENLARGE THE ECONOMIC OPPORTUNITIES OF THE DIFFERENTLY-ABL ED AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale: The bill goes a step further than these laws by giving the disabled more opportunities to be part of the labor workforce, uplifting their dignity and morale by letting them bring in their own contribution s to the community. Since government has, time and again, expressed its commitment to support the disabled, it is but proper and fitting that it start with its various instrumentaliti es thereof. Thus, the passage of this bill is earnestly soughtto effect the government and the legislature's commitment to the sector. >Defines "VENDING FACILITY" as any automatic vending machine and other appropriate auxiliary equipment necessary for the sale of food or beverages and other articles or services dispersed automatically or manually.. > Provides for areas of concern, such as: (1) Designation of and function of the licensing agency; (2) Operation of vending facilities; (3) Issuance of license; (4) Exceptions, etc.

rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING SECTION 443, CHAPTER 2, BOOK III OF THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE OF 1991 TO INCLUDE THE POSITION OF THE MUNICIPAL SOCIAL WELFARE AND DEVELOPMENT OFFICER MANDATORY AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale: From all indications, the position of MUNICIPAL SOCIAL WELFARE AND DEVELOPMENT OFFICER (MSWDO) should be co-opted with the other mandatory positions in the organizational structure of the municipal government. Relegating it to an optionalposition is short of leaving out where credit is due, more so now that among government's focus is in the institutionaliz ation of its anti-poverty program, social reform agenda and the human development where the Municipal Social Welfare Development Officer's role is essential.

rows.title_full: AN ACT TO FURTHER AMEND ACT NO. 2655, AS AMENDED, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE USURY LAW AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale: Commonwealth Act Number 2655, more commonly known as the Usury Law was put out statute books to eradicate a virulent social cancer, which was to prevent the imposition of exorbitant or unreasonable interest rates. However, due to the amendments made upon the Usury Law by Presidential Decrees 116 and 1684, this social legislation lost its effectiveness. The amendments empowered the Monetary Board to impose ceiling on the interest rates that lenders are allowed under various sections of the Usury Law. However, under the present state of the law, the Monetary Board did not place any ceiling on the interest rates. Without these ceilings, any interest rate had become legally binding between the lender and the borrower. Seeks, therefoore, to AMEND  the Usury Law with the following amendment: "SECTION 1. The rate of interest for loans or forbearance of any money, goods, or credits and the rate allowed in judgments, in the absence of express contract as to such rate of interest, sh

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROHIBITING THE GLORIFICATION OF GUNS AND VIOLENCE IN MOVIE, TELEVISION, RADIO, PRINT MEDIA AND OTHER SIMILAR MEDIUM AND PROVIDING PENALTIES FOR VIOLATION THEREOF
rows.abstract: Rationale: "... it is imperative to prohibit the glorification of guns and violence in movies, television, radio and print media to protect the youth who are very susceptible to following the footsteps of their movie idols and to avoid undue influence on mature individuals." >Defines the term "GLORIFICATION" as the portrayal of the use of guns or the act of violence as an approved and accepted normal or ordinary way of life, or when the presentation is given a favorable aspect, dignifying the violent act and showing that its portrayal is worthy of praise and emulation. >Prescribes penalties for glorifying guns and violence with a fine of not less than P20,000.00, but not more than P50,000.00, or by imprisonment.

rows.abstract: "National Environmental Education Act of 1997" Creates the OFFICE OF ENVIRONMENTAL EDUCATION which shall serve as the primary government agency responsible for the environmnetal education and training of all sectors of society. Mandates said Officeto --- (1) develop and implement a national integrated and comprehensive action plan for environmental education and training; (2) formulate and prescribe an expanded and varied program of curriculum development to include value formationa and behavioral change on environmental concerns and issues for schools, colleges and universities; (3) design and conduct massive information dissemination campaign and environmental education and training programs; and (4) depitize or request the assistance oof appropriate government agencies, local goverment units and non-governmenta l organizations for the purpose of implementing this Act.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on ECOLOGY since 1997-08-11

rows.author: A053
rows.title_full: AN ACT INSTITUTING A NATIONAL DRUG TESTING ACT AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract: Rationale: In the 1997 State of the Nation Address (SONA), the government declared an all-out war against the drug menace in the country. It has been noted, however, that among the nation's 5.7 million high school and college students, at least 365,000 of them are hooked to drugs, while an estimated 570,000 students are exprimenting with the substances. >Despite the reimposition of the death penalty and the dangers associated with the drug trade, this illegal indsutry continues to flourish. Defines "DRUG TESTING" as referring to testing and evaluative procedures whether physical, chemical, physiological or otherwise conducted by qualified health personnel and law-enforcement officers to determine whether the subject has taken or is using pprohibited or regulated drugs and substances. > Provides for these areas of concern: (1) Concerned and Implementing Agencies; (2) Jurisdiction; (3) Implementting Rules and Regulations; and (4) Penalties.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HEALTH since 1997-08-11

rows.author: A081
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING THAT ANOTHER PRELIMINARY INVESTIGATION AND REVIEW SHALL BE AVAILABLE FROM RESOLUTIONS OF DISMISSAL PROMULGATED BY THE CITY, PROVINCIAL OR STATE PROSECUTORS
rows.abstract: Rationale: It is undeniable that prosecutors are among the pillars of our criminal justice system.  They are the ones who determine the criminal liability of an accused in a complainant. However, sometimes these prosecutors, for one reason or another, fail to appreciate the pieces of evidence presented by the complainant therey dismissing the complainant. Under our existing laws, a resolution of dismissal leaveas the complaint without a recourse but to accept the prosecutor's resolution of thecase, while the defendant who may have been actually guilty will be able to evade the sanction for this wrong doing and laugh his way out of the prosecution office. > Declares the following --- "SECTION 1. Any provision of existing laws, rules or reggulations to the contrary notwithstanding , a resolution dismissing a complaint promulgated by a city, provincial or state prosecutor may, on motion of the complaint, be subject of another preliminary investigation by the psoecutor concerned."
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on JUSTICE since 1997-08-12

rows.abstract: Declares the following --- "SECTION 1. Any law, decree and rule and regulation to the contrary notwithstanding , the normal height of a Filipino is hereby established as the prescribed minimum requirement for admission to the police and military service.  For this purpose, the Department of Health shall determine as soon as practicable, the necessity of height prescription in the admission to police or military service."

rows.author: A102
rows.title_full: AN ACT ENHANCING FURTHER WORKERS' WELFARE BY PROHIBITING AND CRIMINALIZING 'BOUNDARY SYSTEM' AND SIMILAR SCHEMES IN TAXI AND OTHER PUBLIC TRANSPORT COMPANIES
rows.abstract: Rationale: 'Boundary system' is a system whereby a franchise operator of let us say, jeepneys, rents out his jeepney to a driver, at say P30.00 a day. The owner (operator) expects to collect from the driver his P30.00 at the end of the day.  Any earning over and above the P30.00 (the boundary) goes to the driver. So the bigger the earnings over and above the boundary, as in this example, the better for the driver. > This is the reason why drivers, under this boundary agreement , are apt to drive faster and always on the go, for the more trips they make in a day, the bigger their earnings. This rush maneuver or operation, however, almost always results in accidents unfortunately.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on TRANSPORTATION AND COMMUNICATIONS since 1997-08-12

rows.author: B048
rows.title_full: AN ACT REQUIRING CANDIDATES FOR ALL ELECTIVE PUBLIC OFFICE TO SUBMIT CERTIFICATE OF NEUROLOGICAL TEST AND DRUG TEST AS ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS FOR THE FILING OF CERTIFICATE OF CANDIDACY, AMENDING BATAS PAMBANSA BLG. 811, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE OMNIBUS ELECTION CODE AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale: Section 7, Artilce 3 of our Constitution provides that it is the right of the people to information on matters of public concern. Health and the physiological frameup of an aspirant to an elective position are concededly  a matter of public concern. These two aspects of man are the foundation of his action, the cause, if not the primary source, of our efficiency. > Amends, therefore, the Omnibus Election Code to read as follows: "SECTION 73. Certificate of Candidacy. - No person shall be eligible for any elective public office unless he files a sworn Certificate of Candidacy TOGETHER WITH THE RESULT OF A NEUROLOGICAL EXAMINATION CONDUCTED BY AN ACCREDITED LICENSED NEUROLOGIST AND A CERTIFICATE FROM THE PNP CRIME LABORATORIES ATTTESTING TO THE RESULT OF A DRUG TEST ON THE ASPIRANT, within the period fixed herein. > THE RESULT OF THE NEUROLOGICAL EXAMINATION AND THE DRUG TEST SHALL BE INADMISSIBLE FOR ANY PURPOSE IN ANY PROCEEDING.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on SUFFRAGE AND ELECTORAL REFORMS since 1997-08-12

rows.author: A090
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROHIBITING THE PRACTICE OF HUMAN CLONING AND OPERATION OF ESTABLISHMENT OR INSTITUTION ENGAGED IN THE SAME IN THE PHILIPPINES AND IMPOSING PENALTY THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale: The recent issue on cloning of animals by scientists has stirred controversial views amongst, medical, religious and social groups internationally . With this breakthrough of cloning animals, cloning of human beings is possible and can beprobably achieved in similar ways. The practice of human clooning is considered as unethical, unconstitutiona l, tampering and interfering with God's original creation. > Penalizes violation of this Act with a fine of P600,000.00, or imprisonment for a period of six (6) years, or both.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY since 1997-08-13

rows.author: A090
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROHIBITING THE ACCESS OF PORNOGRAPHIC AND SMUT WEB SITES THROUGH THE INTERNET IN PUBLIC PLACES AND PROVIDING PENALTIES THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale: This bill seeks to prohibit any person from accessing a pornographic web site for whatever purpose in public places such as parks, canteens, theaters, classrooms, computer rental shops, school, colleges and universities and other similarplaces.  This bill aims to protect and preserve the moral virtues and culture of our youth against smut and pornography. It also wants to give protection to other people against nuisance, offensive and obnoxious individuals. >Penalizes violation of this Act with a fine of P5,000.00, or imprisonment of five (5) years, or both.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on PUBLIC INFORMATION since 1997-08-13
